title: Getting started with R3DFEM
text: run_batch() runs set simulations, one per row data.frame, directory copy inputs. columns arguments run_3DCMCCFEM() (parameters species file, see ); inputdir can change run run. parallel = TRUE simulations run future plan set user: outputs runs can read together: Columns named species parameters change parameterization run. param_sensitivity() uses show effect parameter:
code: sites <- system.file("extdata", c("bilykriz/rcp0p0", "hyytiala", "soro"), package = "R3DFEM") runs <- data.frame(id = c("bilykriz", "hyytiala", "soroe"),                    site = c("BilyKriz", "Hyytiala", "Soroe"),                    species = c("Piceaabies", "Pinussylvestris", "Fagussylvatica"),                    inputdir = sites)  future::plan("multisession", workers = 3) res <- run_batch(runs, outputdir = file.path(out, "sites"), year_start = 1997,                  year_end = 2050, man = "off", output = "annual", parallel = TRUE) future::plan("sequential") res[, c("id", "status")] #>         id status #> 1 bilykriz     ok #> 2 hyytiala     ok #> 3    soroe     ok all <- read_output(res$output) all$site <- basename(dirname(dirname(all$file))) ggplot2::ggplot(all, ggplot2::aes(YEAR, NPP, colour = site)) +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   ggplot2::theme_classic() s <- param_sensitivity("LIGHT_TOL", value = 1:4, variable = c("GPP", "HEIGHT"),                        inputdir = bk, outputdir = file.path(out, "sens"),                        site = "BilyKriz", species = "Piceaabies",                        year_start = 1997, year_end = 2050, man = "off") s$plot

title: R Wrapper for the 3D-CMCC-FEM Forest Model (Version 5.7)
text: , present schematic description input needed functions R package: initialization, 3D-CMCC-FEM requires input data: initial stand conditions: species name (since model parameterized species level), age, mean tree height, diameter breast height (DBH), number trees per size cell. initial data aggregated per classes (height classes, cohorts, species) pre-processing activity follows: (1) relative values diameters class associated species, (2) corresponding value height class assigned diameter class, (3) relative age assigned height class (Collalti et al., 2014; 2024). Species-specific parameters primarily based species-specific eco-physiological allometric characteristics can partially derived forest inventories literature (Collalti et al., 2019). package comes parameterizations version 5.7 common European tree species (list_species()), used many real case studies across Europe. Meteorological forcing data: daily maximum (Tmax, °C) minimum air temperature (Tmin, °C), soil temperature (Tsoil, °C), vapor pressure deficit (hPa), global solar radiation (MJ m−2 day−1) precipitation amount (mm day−1). Annual atmospheric CO2 concentration nitrogen deposition (optional)(Collalti et al., 2018). Soil topographic information: soil depth, average sand, clay, silt percentages, elevation. input data need written separate .txt files whose structure fully described user manual. Based input files argument set, function wrapping model (run_3DCMCCFEM) creates setting file input directory used internal C code; user need interact setting file. main output variables 3D-CMCC-FEM (either daily, monthly, annual scale) Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), Net Primary Productivity (NPP), state variables evapotranspiration (ET), Leaf Area Index (LAI), rain interception (cite ). Results obtained either class level (species, diameter, height, age class level), layer level (sum tree height classes layer), grid level (sum classes different layers). model provides information support decision-making forest management planning, mean annual volume increment (MAI), current volume increment (CAI), basal area, DBH. detailed information 3D-CMCC-FEM applications, strongly encourage refer literature (Collalti et al., 2014, 2016, 2020, 2024; Marconi et al., 2017; Mahnken et al., 2022; Dalmonech et al., 2022, 2024; Testolin et al., 2023; Vangi et al., 2024a, 2024b; Morichetti et al., 2024), main web page, updated user guide can found (include detailed description inputs outputs, well instruction launching model command line, Eclipse Bash; Collalti et al., 2022).
